newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch TV producer Endemol targets foreign expansio.
newsitem.headline: Dutch TV producer Endemol targets foreign expansio.

text.p: Dutch television production firm Endemol Entertainment said on Friday it would continue to focus on expansion outside its core Dutch and German markets.
"Foreign markets are becoming increasingly important for us," co-chairman John de Mol told a news conference.
De Mol noted that over 40 percent of the company's television programming turnover was already generated outside the Netherlands, with some 30 percent coming from Germany alone.
"All the other European countries together contribute only 11 percent. I say 'only' because that is where we believe our best prospects for growth lie," he said.
Formed in 1994 through a merger of the production firms of joint chairmen Joop van den Ende and John de Mol, Endemol plans a partial flotation on the Amsterdam bourse later this year.
The company specialises in the production of popular game shows, soap operas and drama series.

Its main television operations outside the Netherlands include wholly-owned production subsidiaries in Germany and Portugal as well as joint ventures in Spain and France in which it holds stakes of 40 and 50 percent respectively.
De Mol said Endemol viewed eastern Europe as one of the most promising growth markets.

Endemol is optimistic about the opportunities throughout Europe as the ending of state monopolies leads to the growth of independent TV channels who are increasingly looking to replace cheap imported U.S. shows with programmes in their own language.
"We see growth of the television market in Europe because the market is maturing. There is a growing need for locally produced prime-time amusement," De Mol said.
Endemol also plans to expand its live entertainment business, in some cases through co-productions with foreign partners, he said.

Live entertainment currently accounts for 21 percent of total turnover. Earlier this year Endemol acquired the Holiday on Ice entertainment firm which stages some 1,700 ice-skating shows a year around the world.
The other main pillar of the live entertainment division is the production of Broadway- or West End-style musicals.
Endemol's stage production of the Dutch version of the Phantom of the Opera ran for an unprecedented three years.
De Mol said Endemol's Dutch version of Miss Saigon would open in six weeks, adding that advance ticket sales were double those for the Phantom six weeks before that show opened.
